commit_message:
[turbofan] Reduce the amount of map loads during elements kind transitions

Adopt the "TransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap" concept from Maglev. It
allows us to do only one map load instead of one map load per transition.

findings.title: Missing kUnreliableMaps in TransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap case of InferMapsUnsafe
findings.message: In `NodeProperties::InferMapsUnsafe`, the newly introduced `case IrOpcode::kTransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap` only updates `*maps_out` and returns when `receiver` and `object` are identical via `IsSame()`. When they are not identical (the `else` path), it silently `break`s without setting `result = kUnreliableMaps`. Because `receiver` and `object` may still alias at runtime (pointing to the same heap object through different SSA paths/phi nodes), the `TransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap` operation can change the receiver's map even when `IsSame()` returns false. Callers of `InferMapsUnsafe` then receive stale/incorrect map information and proceed with optimizations that assume an impossible type, triggering a SIGTRAP (debug assertion) in the compiled code.
findings.suggestion: Before the `break` in the `kTransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap` case, add `result = kUnreliableMaps;` to indicate that any previously inferred maps for the receiver are no longer reliable, because the aliasing object's map may have been transitioned.

ground_truth.root_cause: The new `kTransitionElementsKindOrCheckMap` case in `InferMapsUnsafe` only considers the trivial aliasing case (`IsSame`). It neglects the possibility of non-trivial aliasing (same heap object reachable via different SSA value paths). Other opcodes in the same function that can have side effects on aliasing objects correctly set `result = kUnreliableMaps` before breaking; the new case was missing this defensive assignment.
